pr_body:
See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/65228#issuecomment-1338859262

`duplicate()` and `duplicate_from_editor()` are a bit different, but *hopefully* it doesn't matter that much when saving a scene. I think the only way to call `_save_node()` outside editor builds is to send a custom message to the debugger.

- Fixes #69663
pr_comments: Thanks for fixing this; The CI doesn't do `template_debug` builds currently, and this would have been caught if it were so. Consider adding it to the matrix?

issue_context.title: Can't compile debug template on latest master
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.beta.custom_build [43e9ca40f]

### System information

Manjaro Linux

### Issue description

Fails to compile with:

`scene/debugger/scene_debugger.cpp: In static member function 'static void SceneDebugger::_save_node(ObjectID, const String&)':
scene/debugger/scene_debugger.cpp:224:28: error: 'class Node' has no member named 'duplicate_from_editor'
  224 |         Node *copy = node->duplicate_from_editor(duplimap);
      |                            ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`

### Steps to reproduce

just compile with  `scons target=template_debug arch=x86_64 -j "$(nproc)"`

### Minimal reproduction project

Not needed
comments: Regression from #65228, should be fixed by #69658.

review_comments:
You don't need `duplimap` in template build, so it can go inside the `TOOLS_ENABLED`.

Though it's not used *at all*, so you could check if the method supports just passing a nullptr instead of allocating and filling a hashmap for nothing.
It can't be null, because it's passed as reference.
Looks like it still needs to be defined in the scope first to be passed as reference.

But the same code is used in `duplicate_from_editor()` :/ (it's an overload for method that takes 2 hashmaps)
EDIT:
Ah, the other one is const...
